r: **Seuna (Sevuna) Yadavas** of Devagiri; ruled the western Deccan (Maharashtra) c. **1187–1317**
First **feudatories of the Western (Kalyani) Chalukyas** (and earlier the Rashtrakutas)
**Marathi** – the Yadavas **encouraged Marathi**; **Sanskrit** = language of scholarship
**Bhillama V** – threw off Kalyani Chalukya rule and built **Devagiri** (c. **1187**) as capital
Name given to Devagiri by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** when he shifted his capital there (**1327**)
Founder; built Devagiri; beaten by Hoysala Veera Ballala II
**Killed Kakatiya Rudradeva**; held young Ganapatideva captive, released him (1199) and married his daughter **Somaladevi** to him
**Greatest Yadava**; title **Teluguraya Sthapanacharya**; defeated the Hoysalas; son **Sarangapanideva** later served at Rudramadevi's court
His attack on the Kakatiyas was **repulsed by Rudramadevi**
Ruler at **Alauddin Khalji's 1296 raid**; later a vassal
**Jaitugi** – recorded by Hemadri and confirmed by the **Paithan copper plate** of Ramachandra
As a counterweight to Hoysala **Veera Ballala II's** push into the **Krishna–Tungabhadra** region

**First Muslim invasion of the South**: Alauddin Khalji, then governor of Kara under Sultan Jalaluddin, raids Devagiri and defeats **Ramachandra**; promised the yearly revenue of **Ellichpur** but did not send it
**Malik Kafur**: **Ramachandra** submits and is taken to Delhi, then restored as a vassal
**Malik Burhanuddin** of Devagiri given charge of Andhra; Devagiri = the Sultanate's Deccan base

2.x: **Significance:** Devagiri was the **first southern kingdom to fall** to Delhi and opened the road to Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.

r: Sanskrit encyclopaedia by **Hemadri** – on **dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas**
**Shrikaranadhipa** (head of secretariat and records) under **Mahadeva and Ramachandra**
Claimed that **Jaitugi captured and sacrificed Rudra**
Credited to Hemadri – local **black basalt**, dressed stones **interlocked without mortar** (**dry masonry**)
Court musician of **Singhana II**; **Sangita Ratnakara** – base text of both Hindustani and Carnatic music
Court astronomer of Singhana II; **grandson of Bhaskaracharya**; school at **Patan** to teach Bhaskara's works
**Dnyaneshwari** – Marathi commentary on the **Bhagavad Gita**, **1290**, Nevasa, in **Ramachandra's** reign

1.x: Later Bhakti saints Namdev, Tukaram and Ramdas carried Upanishad and Gita ideas into Marathi.

r: From the **Yadu** clan of Krishna (Dvaravati / Dwaraka) – hence "Yadavas"; their own records call them **Seunas**
**Dridhaprahara** (c. 860), capital **Chandradityapura (Chandor, Nashik district)** – feudatory of the **Rashtrakutas**
Gave the name **Seunadesha** (Khandesh – Nashik region); founded **Seunapura** near **Sinnar**
The **Kalachuri usurpation (Bijjala)** at Kalyani weakened the Chalukyas; **Bhillama V** founded the independent kingdom at **Devagiri (1187)**
Hoysalas (south), **Kakatiyas** (east), **Paramaras of Malwa** and **Vaghelas / Chaulukyas of Gujarat** (north), **Shilaharas of Kolhapur** (south-west)
**Singhana II** annexed the **Shilahara kingdom of Kolhapur** and raided Gujarat and Malwa
Of Devagiri – financed his **murder of Jalaluddin Khalji and seizure of the Delhi throne** the same year
Rock-cut, moated hill fort begun under Bhillama V; renamed **Daulatabad** by Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1327)
Yadava-period **panchayatana** Shiva temple in the **Bhumija** style
Local black basalt, dry masonry without mortar; spread across **Marathwada and Vidarbha** – the Yadava heartland
Credited by tradition with popularising the **Modi script** (cursive Marathi); commentary on *Ashtanga Hridaya* (Ayurveda)
Sanskrit grammarian, author of ***Mugdhabodha***; protégé of Hemadri
Also wrote ***Amritanubhav***; **samadhi at Alandi (1296)**; founding saint of the **Varkari** tradition
Devotion to **Vithoba (Vitthal) of Pandharpur**; annual **wari** pilgrimage; saints **Namdev, Janabai, Muktabai, Gora Kumbhar, Chokhamela** – Dnyaneshwar's contemporaries
His hymns are in the **Guru Granth Sahib**
Founded **1267** by **Chakradhar Swami**; worships **Krishna / Dattatreya**; rejects caste and rituals; writes in **Marathi**
Early Yadava inscriptions mostly in **Kannada**; from the 13th century **Marathi** records and literature grow
